article_title: How to Improve the Explanatory Power of an Intelligent Textbook: a Case Study in Legal Writing
citation: Sovrano Francesco, Ashley Kevin, Brusilovsky Peter Leonid, Vitali Fabio. (2024). How to Improve the Explanatory Power of an Intelligent Textbook: a Case Study in Legal Writing. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-024-00399-w
title: YAI4Edu: a pipeline that converts static e-books into interactive intelligent textbooks with open-ended questioning and overviewing
description: YAI4Edu is an extension of YAI4Hu that automatically transforms static educative e-books in PDF, XML or HTML format into interactive intelligent textbooks. Interaction is given by "i) word glosses that can be clicked to open an overview; ii) a special kind of search box that allows the reader to get answers to any open-ended English question." It extracts a knowledge graph of template-triplets formatted as RDF from a collection of texts and retrieves answers via embedding similarity using a MiniLM-based model. Source code and anonymized evaluation data are released under MIT license at https://github.com/Francesco-Sovrano/YAI4Edu.
requirements: A collection of texts integrating the textbook (e.g., an encyclopedia) from which to extract the knowledge graph
Hyper-parameters for the Intelligent Explanation Generator (k=10, p=.57, L=50, s=.95, q=4, a=2 in the case study)
constraints: The extracted knowledge graph is imperfect because of the adopted extraction procedure and may contain mistakes from wrongly identified grammatical dependencies
target_learners: University students in an interdisciplinary legal analytics and AI course
target_learning_goals: Learning how to write a legal memorandum in the U.S. legal system
examples: Applied to 22 textbook pages, 5,407 legal-encyclopedia web pages, and 11,198 BVA legal cases, producing an interactive annotated version of the textbook
